newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-CAMPESE TO RETIRE FROM INTERNATIONAL GAME.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-CAMPESE TO RETIRE FROM INTERNATIONAL GAME.

text.p: David Campese will retire from international rugby after winning his 101st cap for Australia against Wales on Sunday.
"This will definitely be my last international appearance -- this has been a tough year -- and I hope that I will be able to bow out in some style," he said on Friday.
Campese's decision to bring the curtain down on a glittering international career will see him enter the history books as one of rugby's all-time greats.
Against Italy last month he became only the second player to make 100 test appearances and he has scored 64 tries during a 14-year career at the top.
He made his test debut against New Zealand in 1982 and has played in three World Cups, including Australia's title-winning display against England at Twickenham in the 1991 final.
Campese is one of four changes to the side who beat Ireland 22-12 last Saturday.
Jason Little moves back into the centre alongside skipper Tim Horan to accommodate Campese, while fly-half Pat Howard takes over from David Knox.
In the forwards, lock Warwick Waugh has a shoulder injury and is replaced by Tim Gavin, while Owen Finegan wins the vote ahead of Daniel Manu in the back row.
Team: M. Burke; J. Roff, J. Little, T. Horan (captain), D. Campese; P. Howard, G. Gregan; D. Crowley, M. Foley, A. Blades, T. Gavin, D. Giffin, O. Finegan, M. Brial, D. Wilson.
